hints: Calculate the acceleration of A down the smooth plane ($a = g \sin \theta = 10 \times 0.2 = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$) and find its speed before collision: $v_A = 2(2) = 4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Apply conservation of momentum along the plane to find the velocity of A after collision: $2.5(4) + 3(-3.5) = 2.5 u + 3(0.5) \implies u = -0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (moving up the plane at $0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$).
Use $v^2 = u^2 + 2as$ with $u = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, $v = 0$, and deceleration $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to find the distance moved up the plane.
walkthrough:
Find the acceleration of A down the smooth incline before collision:
$$a = g \sin \theta = 10 \times 0.2 = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
$$v_A = u + at = 0 + 2(2) = 4\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ (down the plane)}$$

Apply conservation of momentum along the incline (taking down the plane as positive):
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$
$$2.5(4) + 3(-3.5) = 2.5 u + 3(0.5)$$
$$10 - 10.5 = 2.5u + 1.5 \implies -0.5 = 2.5u + 1.5 \implies 2.5u = -2.0 \implies u = -0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

Particle A moves up the plane with initial speed $0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$ against gravity component $a = -g \sin \theta = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ until coming to rest ($v = 0$):
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as \implies 0 = 0.8^2 + 2(-2)s$$
$$4s = 0.64 \implies s = \frac{0.64}{4} = 0.16\text{ m}$$
teacher_walkthrough:
Phase 1: Motion of particle A prior to collision.
Particle A of mass $m_A = 2.5\text{ kg}$ is released from rest ($u = 0$) on a smooth plane inclined at $\theta$ with $\sin \theta = 0.2$.
The acceleration down the plane is:
$$a = g \sin \theta = 10 \times 0.2 = 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
After $t = 2\text{ s}$, its speed immediately before collision is:
$$v_A = u + at = 0 + 2(2) = 4\text{ m s}^{-1} \text{ (directed down the slope)}$$

Phase 2: Direct collision between A and B.
Let down the plane be the positive direction:
- Particle A: $m_A = 2.5\text{ kg}$, $u_A = +4\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
- Particle B: $m_B = 3\text{ kg}$, $u_B = -3.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$ (moving up the slope).
- After collision: B moves down the slope at $v_B = +0.5\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
By conservation of momentum:
$$m_A u_A + m_B u_B = m_A v_A + m_B v_B$$
$$2.5(4) + 3(-3.5) = 2.5 v_A + 3(0.5)$$
$$10 - 10.5 = 2.5 v_A + 1.5$$
$$-0.5 = 2.5 v_A + 1.5$$
$$2.5 v_A = -2.0$$
$$v_A = -0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
Thus, particle A rebounds up the plane with speed $0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Phase 3: Motion of A up the plane until instantaneous rest.
Particle A moves up the smooth plane with initial velocity $u = 0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$. The acceleration opposing this upward motion is $a = -g \sin \theta = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
At the highest point, $v = 0$:
$$v^2 = u^2 + 2as$$
$$0^2 = (0.8)^2 + 2(-2)s$$
$$0 = 0.64 - 4s$$
$$4s = 0.64$$
$$s = 0.16\text{ m}$$

ai_rubric.Conserving Linear Momentum: Finds speed before collision $4\text{ m s}^{-1}$, solves momentum equation to get rebound speed $0.8\text{ m s}^{-1}$, and calculates stopping distance $s = 0.16\text{ m}$.
